member.name: Pip
member.description: A young fox in a keeper's coat far too big for him, sleeves rolled up and hem dragging, carrying a brass lantern.
member.persona: Afraid of the dark, and quietly hoping to be the next keeper. Brave when it counts, and grateful for help.

member.name: Wick
member.description: An old badger keeper in a flat blue cap, blue-grey coat and cream waistcoat, with thick round spectacles and a logbook held close.
member.persona: Grumpy, proud and secretly losing his sight. Gruff on top, tender underneath.

member.name: Moth
member.description: A fluffy moth with a fur collar, feathered antennae and big dark eyes.
member.persona: Flies at anything bright, brings odd finds, and means well.

member.name: Thimble
member.description: A young field mouse in a knitted navy sailor's jersey, with a brass sewing thimble worn as a hat.
member.persona: From the sewing basket, and a sailor at heart. Small, bright and brave, with old-fashioned manners: much obliged.

cues.summary: the book opens and its pages stand up
a gust of wind crosses the page
a carried light blows out
the lighthouse beam sweeps the room
a frightened character lets go of what it carries, and it rolls away
a carried light flares back to life
a character sets down what it holds at its feet
a character puts on what it holds, such as a scarf
the page's corner lifts, inviting the reader to turn it
the pop-ups fold flat, the page turns and the next spread rises
a kite lifts its holder over the gap
the moth carries a thread across and its holder hauls over
a ladder is laid across the gap and crawled over
a rope is thrown across the gap and climbed over
a spark rises from a carried light to the lighthouse lamp
the lighthouse lamp lights
what the reader gave goes into the satchel
the end of the chapter is printed on the page
a rustle in the dark
the lighthouse lamp goes dark
a character tucks what it holds into its coat
a keeper's light goes up high: on a kite, atop a standing ladder, or with Moth
the light comes back down to its keeper, and what held it is set down
the moth carries a thread out to the rock, and the mouse is hauled in on it
a line is thrown out to the rock and the mouse comes in on it
a ladder is laid from the rock to the step and the mouse comes across
the mouse holds a kite tail and the wind carries her in
the sea lifts the mouse and sets her down on the step
a rope is thrown across the gap and the old badger climbs over
a ladder is laid across the gap and the old badger feels his way over
a kite carries the old badger over the gap
